en: Oh, it's you. Carefree as ever, I see.
Or should I say idle?
I'd almost like you to do my job for me.
I have to see to everything, even funding,
so it's truly back-breaking.
Ah, it's you. Keeping well?
I'm keeping well myself.
I've heard a little rumour that you come
from a certain noble family abroad...
How about dinner together sometime?
I'd like to hear about your lineage.
(Vulgar human... How galling...)
Hm? Who are you?
State your business.
You would be Councillor Norman, I take it.
Indeed, I am Norman.
Well, I am supposed to hear out
the public, after all. What is it?
I came to see what sort of place this is.
Just sightseeing?! Unbelievable.
I wasted my time coming out in person.
Do you remember that we have met before?
Hmph. I have more acquaintances than
I can count. I can't be expected to
remember every person I meet in passing.
the public, after all.
note: Shares #5536 'Well, I am supposed to hear out'. Variant with trailing space for msg 227023, where #5605 follows on the same line.

en: If you have something to say, say it.
You again?
I don't give guided tours, you know.
I hear you've been visiting all sorts of
other places as well.
I have a great deal of free time.
So you wander aimlessly all over town,
is that it? London is filling up with odd
people. Hmph.
Don't you ever tire of it? Here again?
Well, you hardly look like a spy or any
such thing. You're far too careless.
Only, I'll ask you not to get in my way.
Could it be that you...
...go about ducking under every roof
you pass because it's cold outside?
...Or not.
What an odd thing for me to think.
And I wasted time thinking it.
I hear you come from a noble family.
I'd love to know which house, and what kind.
We must have a proper talk sometime.
Hm? And who might you be?
Even at home, I make it a rule not to see
anyone without an appointment. Please go.
If you want to talk, see me at my office.
You really do love snooping into other
people's affairs... Is that your job?
Enough of this, or I'll call the police.
Stay away from my house.
I'm actually getting used to seeing you.
If that's your strategy, it's a fine one.
Oh, very well.
Getting to know someone like you
may teach me something, too.
Very well, I'll allow your visits.
But London's important figures also
often show their faces at this house.
Do consider what that means.
Greedy human, no better than a ghoul...
From now on, I'll work you to the bone
note: No speaker tag; the player after enslaving Norman.

en: as my servant.
No, nothing in particular.
I only wanted to say hello.
(What an unpleasant man...)
What is it? I'm in a hurry.
That's right, we've never met.
I make a point of greeting everyone I meet.
Yes, thank you.
Yes, I'd like that. Sometime, then...
(...What's come over him?)
note: Referent inferred: Christopher wonders at Norman's sudden friendliness.

en: You're Councillor Norman, aren't you?
I'm
note: Before the name; next row gives the full stop (#452/#863/#5477/#9695).

en: No, not really...
